The helper functions shared by every study's map. Each takes everything it needs as arguments, so the same function draws the HCV, DCD and machine-perfusion maps.

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

This R script file is itself reliant on the following helper file:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/UNOS-mapping/blob/main/R/setup.R)

The code sections below are imported directly from that script when this page is rendered.
:::

#| include: false

## Joining values to the map

The original code split each spreadsheet's "Region 1: Connecticut, Maine, ..." text into seven state columns and pivoted it long, so that it could be joined to a Census shapefile. sRtr's `UNOS_regions_sf` already records each state's region, so each study's table needs only the region name. Every state takes its region's values. The original code used `inner_join()`, which silently drops a region whose name is spelled differently. This function stops instead and names the missing region.

```{r}
#| label: join-region-values
#| eval: false
```

## Choosing the transplant centers

The HRSA layer that `get_hrsa_transplant_centers()` downloads has one row for each center *and organ*, so a center that transplants five organs appears five times. The function keeps centers that list the organ, then one row per center code (`OTC_CD`). It then applies the original maps' rule for pediatric centers (analysis plan section 5), and drops centers outside the mapped states. Without that last step, a center in Puerto Rico appears in the sea south-east of Florida.

```{r}
#| label: select-adult-centers
#| eval: false
```

## The map, in ggplot2

This replaces the original maps' `geom_sf()` calls with two changes. First, the plot is drawn in `map_crs` (`coord_sf(crs = ...)`) rather than in longitude and latitude, so the country is not stretched east to west. Second, centers are drawn with `geom_sf()` at their true locations; the original `geom_jitter()` moved each point randomly by up to 0.3 degrees, which is about 30 km. Region numbers are placed by code (see [Map geography](map_geography.qmd)) instead of from a spreadsheet of hand-entered positions.

```{r}
#| label: map-regions-ggplot
#| eval: false
```

## The map, in tmap, with a Northeast inset

The New England and Mid-Atlantic states are small and their transplant centers crowd together. tmap's `tm_inset()` draws the same map again, enlarged to the extent of the Northeast regions, in a corner of the main map, and outlines that extent on the main map.

```{r}
#| label: map-regions-tmap
#| eval: false
```
